Its sibling `BlocListener<DashboardCubit, ...>` (dashboard-triggered, added one story later by a spec-8-4 review patch) was given a `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced` flag specifically to stop repeat announcements of the same unresolved error — but that flag is written only by the second listener; the first bypasses it entirely. *Verified*: read both listener bodies directly (lines ~525–602); confirmed the narrative-triggered listener has no reference to `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced`. *Consequence*: tapping "tentar novamente" repeatedly while the narrative keeps failing re-triggers a VoiceOver announcement on every tap — the exact spam the sibling fix exists to prevent, reachable through the other listener. — **adversarial lens**

42	2. **`clearStaleError()` never clears `deleteAccountErrorMessage`.** `account_settings_cubit.dart:278-282`'s `clearStaleError()` — written in spec-8-1/8.3 specifically so a DI-singleton cubit's leftover error text doesn't linger into an unrelated later screen visit — only clears the biometric-toggle `errorMessage` field. `deleteAccountErrorMessage` was added two stories later (8.5) and never got the same treatment; `initState()`'s single call site (`screen.dart:93`) only reaches the older field. *Verified*: read `clearStaleError()`'s body and its one call site; confirmed it checks only `state.errorMessage`. *Consequence*: after a failed "Apagar conta" attempt, leaving Configurações via the back arrow and returning later (no new attempt) still shows the stale deletion-failure message — the exact bug `clearStaleError()` was built to prevent, reproduced for the field added after it. — **independently found by both the adversarial and edge-case-hunter lenses**
43	
44	3. **`deleteAccount()` is the only write method in `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl` with no generation guard.** `setBiometricEnabled`/`setDisplayName` each capture `++_generation`/`++_nameGeneration` and discard a superseded result; `deleteAccount()` (`account_settings_repository_impl.dart:212-213`) is a bare pass-through with no counter at all, despite the class's own doc comment stating "every call captures the generation current at its own start" as its concurrency convention. *Verified*: `grep -n "_generation\|deleteAccount"` on the file — confirmed no counter touches the `deleteAccount` line. *Consequence*: the one new repository method this epic added quietly breaks the class's own stated invariant; a future reader who trusts "every write here is generation-guarded" is wrong specifically for the operation where getting concurrency handling wrong matters most. — **adversarial lens**
45	
46	4. **`deleteAccount()` cubit method has `try`/`finally` with no `catch`.** `account_settings_cubit.dart:465-481`: if `_repository.deleteAccount()` or `_finishSession()` throws instead of resolving to `Either` (nothing currently does, but nothing enforces that — the same caveat `logout()`'s own `try`/`finally` patch already documents for itself), the exception propagates uncaught; `isDeletingAccount` resets via `finally`, but no error is ever shown. *Verified*: read the method body directly — confirmed no `catch` clause exists. — **edge-case-hunter lens**
47	
48	5. **Dashboard aggregate's error card has no retry link; the narrative's does.** `dashboard_chart_section.dart`'s `_errorCard` (story 8.1) renders static text only; `_narrativeSection`'s `ResourceError` branch (story 8.2, same file) explicitly added a "tentar novamente" retry link for a failure of the identical shape. *Verified*: grepped both branches — confirmed no `GestureDetector`/`onTap` in `_errorCard`. *Consequence*: a user whose main chart fails to load has no in-screen recovery path, while the narrative directly below it does, for the same failure class. — **adversarial lens**
49	
50	6. **"Apagar conta" shipped with the same missing-loading-indicator gap "Sair" already had — and didn't log the recurrence.** Spec-8-4's own review found and *explicitly deferred* "Sair" having no loading indicator while `isLoggingOut`. Spec-8-5 then added "Apagar conta" with the identical `onPressed: null`-only pattern and no indicator, and its own Review Findings section never mentions it. *Verified*: read both buttons (`screen.dart` ~614–667) — neither has a `CircularProgressIndicator`; `deferred-work.md`'s spec-8-5 entries contain no matching item. *Disposition*: the underlying gap is the same already-accepted tradeoff (shared `AppButton` primitive has no loading-slot API, no device to visually verify a layout change) — **accept as-is**, same rationale as "Sair"'s own deferral. The actionable lesson is process, not code: a later story reusing a pattern a prior story already deferred should cross-reference the existing deferral instead of leaving a second, unlinked instance of the same gap. — **adversarial lens**
51	
52	7. **`_emptyCard`'s padding wasn't updated by the round-2 "no card-resize" fix that touched its siblings.** Story 8.1's round-2 review fix switched `_loadingCard`/`_errorCard`/`_populatedCard` to `DesignTokens.dashboardCardPadding` (20) specifically so the card wouldn't visibly resize across a loading→data transition — `_emptyCard` (the zero-entries state) was left on `DesignTokens.spacingLg` (24). *Verified*: `grep -n "dashboardCardPadding\|spacingLg"` on the file — confirmed `_emptyCard` at line 113 is the only card-builder still using `spacingLg`. *Consequence*: a first-time user with zero entries sees exactly the card-resize jump the fix was written to eliminate everywhere else. — **adversarial lens**
53	
54	8. **Biometric-toggle and name-save spinners have no `semanticsLabel`; the dashboard's identical spinner does.** Story 8.1 gave the dashboard's `CircularProgressIndicator` an explicit `semanticsLabel` ("Carregando gráfico de evolução") as a dedicated accessibility fix. The two near-identical spinners already on the same merged screen (biometric `isSaving`, name-edit `isSavingName`) have none. *Consequence*: a VoiceOver user saving a name or toggling biometric login gets no spoken in-progress feedback, unlike the dashboard's own loading state on the same screen. — **adversarial lens**
55	
56	9. **Narrative `ResourceData` with a blank/whitespace-only string is an unhandled implicit third state.** The render path (`dashboard_chart_section.dart`) already trims and suppresses a blank narrative string (a dedicated round-2 test covers this); but the two announce-listeners in `account_settings_screen.dart` only check `is ResourceError<String>` — a successful-but-blank response neither renders nor announces, silently falling through both paths. *Verified*: re-read both listener bodies; neither inspects `ResourceData.data` for blankness. Low severity (no crash, no visible defect — the card already handles this correctly), but a genuinely unhandled implicit branch. — **edge-case-hunter lens**
57	
58	10. **`AccountSettingsCubit`'s one-time construction-time read of `currentDisplayName`/`currentEmail` depends on an unenforced boot-ordering assumption.** The cubit reads these fields exactly once, at DI-singleton construction; correctness depends on `main()`'s boot-time `fetchBiometricEnabled()` call having already resolved by the time something first resolves `sl<AccountSettingsCubit>()` — nothing asserts or enforces that ordering. *Disposition*: architectural risk, not a current bug (today's DI wiring satisfies the ordering) — **defer**, revisit if DI bootstrap ever changes (eager registration, splash prefetch, new test harness). — **adversarial lens**
59	
60	11. **A failed boot-time `fetchBiometricEnabled()` leaves the name/email header permanently blank for the session.** `_currentDisplayName`/`_currentEmail` are populated only by piggybacking on a successful boot fetch or a successful `setDisplayName()` call; nothing retries if both of `main.dart`'s one-shot boot attempts fail (e.g., app opened offline). *Disposition*: real but narrow (requires offline app launch) — **defer**, propose retrying the fetch the next time Configurações opens rather than relying solely on the two boot-time attempts. — **adversarial lens**
61	
62	### Already known (recorded during the epic's own story-level reviews; not re-routed)
63	
64	Confirmed still present in the current code; logged in `deferred-work.md` under the relevant `spec-8-*` headings. Listed here only because the verification-gap lens independently re-derived the first one with corroborating detail:
65	
66	- **`clearLocalCache()` not coordinated with in-flight writes/fetches** (`deferred-work.md`, spec-8-4 entry) — the verification-gap lens independently re-confirmed this for `EntriesRepository` (an in-flight `create()`/`retry()` can repopulate the just-cleared box) *and* additionally traced the same shape through `ChatRepository.listSessions()`/`listMessages()` (an in-flight fetch, not just a write, can repopulate the just-cleared chat boxes) — broadening, not replacing, the existing entry. **Action item 12** below proposes folding this broader evidence into the existing `deferred-work.md` entry.
67	- The shared `_finishSession()` re-entry race (logout/deleteAccount/toggleBiometric/confirmEditingName can race each other).
68	- In-memory singleton state (cached name/email, dashboard aggregate, chat session, pending-write tracker) not reset on logout/delete.
69	- `DashboardCubit`/`DashboardNarrativeCubit`'s `confirmedWrites` subscriptions living for the whole app session, not just while mounted.
70	- Vault PIN never cleared on logout (explicitly flagged as ambiguous, not a defect).
71	- `EntriesRepository`/`ChatRepository.clearLocalCache()` using `Failure.malformedResponse` for local-storage faults (pre-existing codebase convention).
72	- No real-DI e2e test for `deleteAccount()`'s full orchestration at the time of spec-8-5's own review — **closed** by the `71b5bdc` closing-snapshot commit, which added exactly this.
73	- `SessionRepositoryImpl.logout()`'s silent `catch (_) {}` (deliberately mirrors an existing same-file convention).
74	- The narrative fetch firing unconditionally regardless of entry count (one harmless extra backend call for 0/1-count users) — explicitly accepted in spec-8-2's own Design Notes as the cost of keeping the two `Resource`s genuinely decoupled.
75	
76	### Aggregate views (architecture, duplication, growth, reconciliation)
77	
78	- **Architecture / layering — clean.** `grep`-verified: no domain-layer file in `dashboard/` or `account/` imports `package:flutter` or anything from a `data/` layer. All new repository methods return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09). `AccountSettingsCubit` depends only on domain-layer repository interfaces (`SessionRepository`, `VaultRepository`, `EntriesRepository`, `ChatRepository`, `AccountSettingsRepository`) — no cross-feature data-layer imports (RNF06). All five backend calls (`dashboard-aggregate-get`, `dashboard-narrative-get`, `account-settings-update`, `account-delete`, `auth-logout`) match `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping exactly, called by name per AGENTS.md's convention. Zero hardcoded visual values introduced (`grep` for `Color(0x`/raw px literals in the epic's new widget files found none).
79	- **God-class / size growth.** `account_settings_screen.dart` grew to 677 lines across all 6 commits in this range (net +538 lines over the epic) with a single `build()` method spanning ~354 lines (biometric toggle + dashboard chart + narrative + profile header + name-edit + logout + delete-account, all inline, each story adding its own section without extraction). `account_settings_cubit.dart` grew to 489 lines (net +343) and now owns four largely-unrelated concerns (biometric toggle, name editing, logout, account deletion) in one class. Each story's own in-diff review correctly judged its *own* increment as reasonable; nothing in the per-story process was positioned to notice the cumulative size. The per-line code quality is good — guards, tests, and provenance comments are consistent throughout, confirmed by direct reading — this is a structural/SRP observation, not a correctness defect. **Disposition: accept as-is for this delivery** (no functional requirement calls for splitting it, and extraction now is a refactor with regression risk, not a bug fix); **propose as a follow-up** if this screen gains a 6th concern.
80	- **Duplication — deliberate, self-documented, by design.** `DashboardCubit`/`DashboardNarrativeCubit` are near-total structural duplicates (`diff` of the two files shows only the obvious renames/type changes) — but each file's own doc comment explicitly cross-references the other and states the mirroring is intentional per frozen Boundaries text ("mirroring `DashboardCubit`'s exact shape"). **Accept as-is** — this is accepted deviation, not an accidental reimplementation from one session not knowing the other existed. The one real cost of the duplication (the identical untested `onError`-handler gap existing in both files) is already tracked in `deferred-work.md`.

80	- **Duplication — deliberate, self-documented, by design.** `DashboardCubit`/`DashboardNarrativeCubit` are near-total structural duplicates (`diff` of the two files shows only the obvious renames/type changes) — but each file's own doc comment explicitly cross-references the other and states the mirroring is intentional per frozen Boundaries text ("mirroring `DashboardCubit`'s exact shape"). **Accept as-is** — this is accepted deviation, not an accidental reimplementation from one session not knowing the other existed. The one real cost of the duplication (the identical untested `onError`-handler gap existing in both files) is already tracked in `deferred-work.md`.
81	- **Spec-to-implementation reconciliation — two real spec bugs caught and fixed, both properly reconciled.** Story 8.1's frozen `>30`-entry condensation algorithm degenerated for `bucketCounts.length < 10` (9 invisible bars + 1 giant bar) — found by review, routed to the human via `AskUserQuestion` (root cause sat inside `<frozen-after-approval>` text), fixed with an explicit Spec Change Log entry (left-pad amendment) per direct human instruction to use technical judgment over the heavier revert-and-replan protocol. Story 8.2's frozen narrative-announcement line was unconditional, in tension with the adjacent "never show narrative for 0/1-count" line — same catch-and-reconcile pattern, same human-routed resolution. Both are exactly the "spec that should be reconciled to reality" case this retro's own catalog describes, and both were *already* reconciled in-story with full evidence trails — no outstanding reconciliation work remains from either.
82	
83	## Behavior verification
84	
85	No device/simulator or CI pipeline exists for this project (AGENTS.md) — narrowed scope, consistent with every story's own Verification section. What was actually exercised in this retro, directly, not from the record alone:
86	
87	- `fvm flutter analyze` — re-ran: **"No issues found!"**
88	- `fvm flutter test` (full suite) — re-ran: **1309/1309 passing**, exactly matching `tests/test-summary.md`'s own final ledger (no drift found this time, unlike the 3 earlier drifts the epic's own stories caught and corrected in-flight).
89	- The project's real-DI e2e suite (`test/features/account/account_settings_flow_e2e_test.dart`, `test/features/dashboard/dashboard_flow_e2e_test.dart`) — the closest thing to an end-to-end behavior check this repo has — exercises the genuine DI graph (`sl<...>()`) with fakes only at the HTTP transport boundary, covering logout, account deletion (happy path, backend failure, double-tap no-op), and dashboard aggregate/narrative fetch+recompute, confirmed read directly as part of the review above.
90	
91	No manual/visual walkthrough was performed (no device/simulator exists) — this is an explicit scope gap, not "checked and clean," same as every story's own Verification section already states.
92	
93	## Previous-retro follow-through
94	
95	No previous retrospective exists for any earlier epic — `sprint-status.yaml` shows `epic-1-retrospective` through `epic-7-retrospective` all still `optional`, none ever run, and there are no `action_items` in the file at all. Nothing to follow through on.
96	
97	## Action items
98	
99	Fix-now items (code-level, proposed — not applied in this retro; the next dev session executes and verifies against the normal `fvm flutter analyze`/`fvm flutter test` gate):
100	
101	1. **Fix the narrative-error announce dedup bypass** — route the narrative-triggered `BlocListener` (finding 1) through the same `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced` state the dashboard-triggered listener already uses, so neither path can re-announce an already-announced, still-failing narrative error. *Owner: dev, next pass on `account_settings_screen.dart`.*
102	2. **Widen `clearStaleError()` to also clear `deleteAccountErrorMessage`** (finding 2), or add a sibling clear call from `initState()`. *Owner: dev.*
103	3. **Give `deleteAccount()` its own generation guard** (finding 3), consistent with `setBiometricEnabled`/`setDisplayName`. *Owner: dev.*
104	4. **Add a `catch` to `deleteAccount()`'s cubit method** (finding 4) so an unexpected throw surfaces an error instead of silently resetting state. *Owner: dev.*
105	5. **Add a retry affordance to the dashboard aggregate's `_errorCard`** (finding 5), matching the narrative section's existing "tentar novamente" link. *Owner: dev.*
106	6. **Fix `_emptyCard`'s padding** (finding 7) to `DesignTokens.dashboardCardPadding`, matching its sibling cards. *Owner: dev — trivial, one-line.*
107	7. **Add `semanticsLabel` to the biometric-toggle and name-save spinners** (finding 8), matching the dashboard chart's existing accessibility treatment. *Owner: dev.*
108	
109	Deferred items (tracked, not blocking, context attached so a later pass doesn't need to re-investigate):
110	
111	8. Finding 6 ("Apagar conta" missing-loading-indicator recurrence) — **accept as-is**, same rationale already on record for "Sair"; cross-reference the two `deferred-work.md`-worthy notes if either is ever revisited.
112	9. Finding 9 (blank/whitespace narrative success falls through both render and announce paths) — low severity; propose treating a blank `ResourceData` the same as the narrative-unavailable case if ever touched again.
113	10. Finding 10 (unenforced boot-ordering assumption behind `currentDisplayName`/`currentEmail`'s one-time read) — revisit only if DI bootstrap ordering changes.
114	11. Finding 11 (no retry for a failed boot-time name/email fetch) — revisit if offline-launch UX becomes a priority.
115	12. **Broaden `deferred-work.md`'s existing spec-8-4 `clearLocalCache()`-race entry** to explicitly name `ChatRepository.listSessions()`/`listMessages()` repopulation alongside the already-named `create()`/`sendMessage()`/`retryMessage()` — the verification-gap lens traced the fetch-side (not just write-side) manifestation with concrete evidence this retro's Findings section records. *Owner: dev — documentation-only update to the existing ledger entry, not new code.*
116	
117	Process lessons (what would prevent the next one — no action required unless a future epic recurs):
118	
119	- **A later story adding a second guard/listener for a concern a prior story already partially solved should diff against the sibling, not just review its own new code.** Findings 1 and 8 are both this shape: a later story's accessibility/dedup fix was added without checking whether an earlier story's own near-identical control already needed, or already had, the same treatment. The per-story 4-layer review process is excellent at catching defects in a story's own diff; it has no step that asks "does a sibling control on this same merged screen already have this, or need this too?" — worth adding as an explicit check the next time a story extends an existing shared screen/cubit rather than building a new one.
120	- **A story that re-ships an already-deferred gap under a different name should log the recurrence, not leave it silent.** Finding 6 (spec-8-5 reproducing spec-8-4's own already-deferred "no loading indicator" gap without mentioning it) is low-impact here because the underlying disposition is correctly "accept as-is" either way — but the pattern is worth naming: a recurrence of a *known* gap is cheap to flag with one cross-referencing sentence and easy to miss silently once code review assumes "this is new, not a repeat."
121	- **Worth keeping, not fixing**: the human-routed spec-amendment path (Spec Change Log entries for stories 8.1 and 8.2) worked exactly as intended — two genuinely wrong pieces of *frozen, previously-approved* spec text were caught by post-implementation review, routed to the human via `AskUserQuestion` rather than silently patched or silently left broken, and resolved with an explicit, evidenced amendment plus a "KEEP" list protecting everything that was already correct. This is the retrospective's own job (catching what no single session could see) already happening *inside* the epic, one story at a time — the fact that two such catches were needed in one five-story epic is itself worth noting for anyone estimating how often frozen spec text needs this safety valve.
122	
123	## Acceptance verdict
124	
125	**accepted-with-open-items** (criteria profiled, not declared — epic 8 has no dedicated acceptance-criteria document beyond `epics.md`'s own per-story Given/When/Then text, which this retro treated as the criteria to profile against).
126	
127	Evidence for "criteria met":
128	- All three dashboard entry-count states (0/1/>30) implemented, tested, and the one algorithmic defect in the >30 condensation found and fixed in-story with an evidenced spec amendment.
129	- Narrative text ships as a genuinely independent fetch (never coupled to the chart `Resource`), with a distinct narrative-unavailable state — confirmed by direct code read, not just the spec's own claim.
130	- Inline name editing matches every I/O-matrix row (pencil→check, save, tap-away revert, failure-keeps-draft) with dedicated widget tests for each.
131	- Logout calls `auth-logout`, routes to the vault/login screen, and clears both the entries and chat Hive caches (closing the pre-existing shared-device data-leak gap this epic's own spec named as a goal).
132	- Account deletion uses the destructive-variant red-title dialog, hard-deletes via `DELETE /account`, routes to the same destination as logout, and traps focus while the dialog is open — all confirmed present in code.
133	- `fvm flutter analyze`: zero issues. `fvm flutter test`: 1309/1309 passing, re-verified directly in this retro.
134	- No Clean Architecture, RNF06, RNF09, or design-token violations found anywhere in the epic's diff.
135	
136	Evidence for "open items, not blocking": 11 new findings (1 real correctness bug surfaced to users — the announce-dedup bypass, finding 1 — the rest are consistency/accessibility/architectural-risk items of lesser severity), none of which represent a failure to deliver the epic's own stated functionality. No unfinished stories (`pending_stories` empty). No finding rises to "criteria not met."
137	
138	## Open questions
139	
140	- Should the already-accepted "no loading indicator on Sair/Apagar conta" gap (findings/deferred item 6, 8) be revisited now that it has recurred twice in the same epic, or does the existing rationale (shared `AppButton` has no loading-slot API, no device to visually verify) still hold? This is a product/design call, not something this retro can resolve on its own.
141	- Is the offline-boot name/email-blank gap (deferred item 11) worth a fix now, or is it acceptable given the app's general assumption of connectivity at launch? No `docs/input/` text addresses offline-launch UX directly.
142	
143	---
144	*Retrospective generated via bmad-retrospective. Diff range `6548fec^..71b5bdc`. Review lenses: adversarial, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap (parallel subagents, each independently spot-verified against source before being kept).*

## 3. Visual system (tokens for `design_tokens.dart`)

The prototype has a **Design Tokens** panel, marked as the ground truth for `design_tokens.dart`. Its names and values are below.

### Colors
| Token | Hex | Use (as stated in the panel) |
|---|---|---|
| `colorPrimary` | `#1F3D34` | Buttons, app bar, wordmark |
| `colorPrimaryPressed` | `#16281F` | Pressed state |
| `colorOnPrimary` | `#F5F1E8` | Text on primary |
| `colorAccent` | `#C98A3E` | CTA, insight, saved bookmark |
| `colorOnAccent` | `#241C0D` | Text on accent |
| `colorSecondary` | `#7C8B6F` | Tags, chips, synchronizing |
| `colorSurfaceBg` | `#F2EFE7` | General background ("paper") |
| `colorSurfaceElevated` | `#FBF9F4` | Cards, bubbles, sheets |
| `colorBorder` | `#E1DACB` | Dividers, borders |
| `colorTextPrimary` | `#241F19` | Main text |
| `colorTextSecondary` | `#6B6255` | Secondary text |
| `colorError` | `#B3402A` | Errors, destructive action |
| `colorSuccess` | `#4C6B4F` | Synchronized, confirmations |
| `colorWarningSync` | `#C98A3E` | "Synchronizing" badge |
| `colorInfoOffline` | `#5C7A93` | Offline banner — single use |

Other colors that appear on specific screens but not in the panel: user chat bubble `#D9DFD3`; text on category chips `#3F4A38`.

### Typography
| Token | Font · weight · size/line-height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `textDisplayLg` | Fraunces 600 · 32/38 | Splash wordmark |
| `textHeadlineMd` | Fraunces 600 · 24/30 | Section titles |
| `textTitleLg` | Karla 700 · 20/26 | App bar title |
| `textTitleSm` | Karla 700 · 16/22 | Subtitles |
| `textBodyLg` | Karla 400 · 16/24 | Bubbles, entries |
| `textBodyMd` | Karla 400 · 14/20 | Secondary text and descriptions |
| `textLabelMd` | Karla 500 · 13/18 | Button text, chips |
| `textMonoCaption` | IBM Plex Mono 500 · 12/16 · letter-spacing .2 | Technical metadata (timestamps, counters, status labels) |

### Spacing (4 dp grid)
`spacingXs` 4 · `spacingSm` 8 · `spacingMd` 16 · `spacingLg` 24 · `spacingXl` 32 · `spacing2xl` 48 (dp).

### Radii
`radiusSm` 8 dp (inputs, chips) · `radiusMd` 16 dp (cards, bubbles) · `radiusLg` 24 dp (sheets, modals) · `radiusFull` 999 dp (avatars, pills).

### Elevation
`elevation1` — `0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)` (cards at rest) · `elevation2` — `0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)` (sheets, modals).

### Icons
Phosphor library, Regular style, 24 dp: `list`, `plus`, `magnifying-glass`, `funnel`, `bookmark-simple`, `microphone`, `camera`, `gear`, `kanban`, `notebook`, `fingerprint`, `lightbulb` (and others used on specific screens: `check`, `warning-circle`, `wifi-slash`, `circle-notch`, `caret-left`, `download-simple`, `pencil-simple`, `x`, `stop`, `image`, `check-circle`, `chart-line-up`, `backspace`, `lock-key`, `paper-plane-tilt`, `chat-circle-text`).

### Spine (colored bar on the left of a card) — 3 contexts
1. Proactive insight in the chat — ochre.
2. Entry origin in "Meus Registros" — color by type: manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre.
3. Kanban column in "Planos de Ação" — color by column **[ext]**.

### Micro-animations and transitions
- `scrimIn` (0.18 s ease-out): fade of the darkened background when any overlay opens.
- `sheetUp` (0.2 s ease-out): bottom sheets (insertion modal, filter, export) rise from the bottom of the screen.
- Continuous spinner (`spin`, 1 s linear infinite) in every loading state.
- Text streaming: the AI response is revealed progressively, with a blinking cursor at the end while it is "typing".
- PIN: after the 4th digit, a 350 ms pause before navigating.

content.content:
## Epic 1: Foundation & Session Management

Users can create an account, log in, and have their session silently maintained or gracefully recovered; the app shell navigates between all four base surfaces with clear placeholders for what isn't built yet.

### Story 1.1: Project Scaffold, Stack Integration & Core Infrastructure

As a developer,
I want the Flutter project scaffolded with the pinned stack and the `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` integration verified working together in one bootstrap,
So that every feature built afterward has a stable, correctly-wired foundation instead of discovering an integration conflict mid-feature.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a fresh checkout of the repository
**When** `fvm flutter pub get` and the build runner are executed
**Then** the project resolves all pinned dependencies (Flutter 3.47.x family, `flutter_bloc` ^9.1.1, `go_router` ^18.1.1, `dio` ^5.11.1, `hive_ce`/`hive_ce_flutter` ^2.22.0, `get_it` ^9.3.0, `fpdart` ^1.2.0, `freezed`/`freezed_annotation` ^4.0.3, `json_serializable` ^6.15.2, `mocktail` ^1.0.5, `fl_chart` ^1.3.0, `local_auth` ^3.0.2, `flutter_secure_storage` ^11.2.0, `flutter_dotenv` ^6.0.1, `whisper_ggml` ^2.8.1) with no version conflicts.

**Given** the `lib/` directory after scaffolding
**When** inspected
**Then** it matches the Structural Seed exactly: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for the `data/domain/presentation` split.

**Given** a gitignored `.env` holding `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
**When** the app boots
**Then** `flutter_dotenv` loads both values and no secret is hardcoded anywhere in source.

**Given** the DI bootstrap in `lib/core/di/`
**When** the app starts
**Then** exactly one `get_it` instance is registered, `dio` is configured through it, and an integration test proves `flutter_secure_storage` can be read/written through the same bootstrap — verifying the three packages work together before any feature is built on top of them.
**And** the sealed `Failure` hierarchy (AD-3, 14 subtypes) is defined in `lib/core/failure/`, the one retry interceptor (AD-4) retries only the 6 server `retryable:true` codes, and the one URL builder (AD-5) maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` with `apikey` sent on every call.
**And** one shared, table-driven `mocktail` test helper is built in `core/` that drives the 5-write-endpoint × 3-failure-type (timeout, malformed response, no connection) = 15-scenario matrix (RNF09) against a stubbed `ApiClient` — every later story that owns a write endpoint reuses this helper rather than building its own failure-matrix harness.

### Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library

As a developer,
I want the full visual token set and the generic button/text-field components implemented in `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` and a shared widgets layer,
So that every screen built afterward pulls its visual values and basic controls from one source, with zero hardcoded colors/fonts/spacing anywhere else in the app (RNF08).

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** `DESIGN.md`'s frontmatter token set (colors, typography, rounded, spacing)
**When** `design_tokens.dart` is implemented
**Then** every token name matches `DESIGN.md` verbatim (camelCase), and `elevation1`/`elevation2` are defined as literal shadow constants alongside it (UX-DR1).

**Given** the app's single supported configuration
**When** any screen renders
**Then** it is laid out for a fixed 390×844 logical-point portrait frame, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode code path exists anywhere (UX-DR35).

**Given** the primary, secondary, and text/ghost button components
**When** a button is disabled
**Then** it renders `colorBorder` background with `colorTextSecondary` text — never a dimmed opacity of its active state (UX-DR2).

**Given** the text-field component
**When** it is empty, focused, or holding a validation error
**Then** it shows the default, `colorPrimary`-at-1.5px-focused, and `colorError`-bordered states respectively, with no literal color/width defined outside `design_tokens.dart` (UX-DR3).
**And** every control built from these tokens honors Dynamic Type at every size without truncating or clipping (UX-DR22).

### Story 1.3: Account Creation and Login

As a new or returning user,
I want to create an account or log in with my email and password,
So that I can access my private journal.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the Entrar / Criar conta screen in login mode
**When** I submit a valid, registered email and password
**Then** `POST /auth/login` succeeds and I land on Home/Chat with a persisted session.

**Given** the same screen toggled to signup mode
**When** I submit an email and password
**Then** `POST /auth/signup` is called with exactly those two fields — no password-confirmation or display-name field exists anywhere on the screen (UX-DR31, resolves PRD OQ-2).

**Given** an invalid login attempt
**When** the backend returns `AUTH_INVALID`
**Then** the error shows inline under the fields using the text-field's error-border treatment, and the field is never cleared.

**Given** a malformed email
**When** I attempt to submit before any network call
**Then** client-side validation blocks the submit locally where possible, without a round trip.
**And** every call on this screen sends `apikey` plus `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` per AD-5 — never a user token, since signup/login/refresh are the three `security: []` operations.

### Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence

As a returning user,
I want my session refreshed silently or remembered across app restarts,
So that I don't have to log in every time I open the app.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a previously authenticated session with a valid, unexpired token
**When** I restart the app
**Then** I land on Home/Chat without being re-prompted for credentials.

**Given** a session nearing or past expiry on app foreground
**When** the app checks session validity
**Then** it calls the session-check/refresh operation silently, with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds the 300ms threshold (RNF01).
**And** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from `features/auth/domain/` and registered once in DI as a singleton (AD-8) — no other code path re-derives session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.

### Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay

As a user whose session has expired while using the app,
I want a "Sessão expirada" overlay that lets me re-authenticate without losing my place,
So that I never lose my context or feel like I'm starting over.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I am on any screen and the backend reports `AUTH_EXPIRED`
**When** the overlay appears
**Then** it renders as a scrim over the current screen (confirmation-dialog component, neutral `colorTextPrimary` title, UX-DR16) — the screen underneath, including scroll position, is preserved, never navigated away from.

**Given** the overlay is visible
**When** I tap "Entrar novamente"
**Then** I am routed to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow (built in Epic 2) — never a full login form.

**Given** the overlay is open
**When** I try to interact with anything underneath the scrim
**Then** focus is trapped on the overlay until it is dismissed or actioned (UX-DR25).
**And** its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography, and it is the only overlay permitted on screen at a time — it never stacks on top of another open overlay (UX-DR27, UX-DR36).

### Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders

As a user,
I want to navigate between Home/Chat, the side menu, Meus Registros, and Configurações from the moment I open the app,
So that the whole app feels complete and navigable even while individual features are still being built.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the app has launched
**When** I open the side menu (☰)
**Then** I can reach Chat Session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, and Planos de Ação — all four destinations resolve to a screen, none 404s or crashes.

**Given** a destination whose RF unit is not yet built
**When** I navigate to it
**Then** it renders a visually distinct, clearly-marked placeholder — never a screen that looks finished but does nothing.

**Given** the Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit extension feature, never implemented per project policy)
**When** I open it
**Then** it is styled with full visual polish per the design tokens — never grayed-out or visibly "unfinished" (UX-DR32) — with no backend calls and no interactive drag/drop logic behind it.
**And** the side-menu avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is implemented here for reuse — not reimplementation — when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (UX-DR13).

## Epic 2: Biometric Authentication Vault

Users unlock the app with Face ID/Touch ID (or PIN fallback) before any personal data is ever shown, with no lockout path and no biometric data ever leaving the device.

### Story 2.1: Biometric/PIN App-Access Gate

As a user,
I want the app to require Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN before showing any of my data,
So that my journal stays private even if someone else picks up my phone.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the app is cold-started or resumed after the idle timeout
**When** the vault gate evaluates
**Then** no screen other than the vault/login screen is reachable until authentication succeeds.

**Given** the `go_router` redirect
**When** it evaluates on any navigation attempt
**Then** it composes exactly two gates in fixed order — `VaultStatus` first, then `SessionStatus` (AD-14) — and neither gate ever makes a network call to validate itself; biometric validation is 100% on-device, so no biometric data or call ever reaches the backend.

**Given** Face ID/Touch ID is available and enabled
**When** I open the app
**Then** the OS biometric prompt appears and, on success, routes me straight to Home/Chat.
**And** `features/vault/domain` exposes a `VaultStatus` stream the same way `features/auth/domain` exposes `SessionStatus` (AD-8 pattern), registered once in DI.

### Story 2.2: Biometric-Failure Fallback to PIN

As a user whose biometric check fails,
I want to fall back to entering a PIN,
So that I'm never locked out of my own journal.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Face ID/Touch ID fails to recognize me
**When** the failure is reported
**Then** "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" appears with a PIN entry path always reachable — never a dead end.

**Given** repeated biometric failures trigger an OS-level lockout
**When** that lockout is detected
**Then** the app routes to its own PIN fallback rather than retrying against the OS.

**Given** the PIN keypad (3×4 grid + backspace, progress dots, structural palette only, UX-DR14)
**When** I enter the 4th digit
**Then** the app auto-advances 350ms later with no explicit "confirm" tap (UX-DR27).
**And** the screen-reader announces the failure transition per the Accessibility Floor (UX-DR21), and the keypad's digits remain legible at the largest Dynamic Type size without truncation (UX-DR22).

### Story 2.3: Fixed 5-Minute Idle Re-Authentication Timeout

As a user,
I want re-authentication required only after 5 minutes backgrounded,
So that casual app-switching doesn't interrupt me but a forgotten unlocked phone stays protected.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the app is backgrounded for less than 5 minutes
**When** I resume it
**Then** no re-authentication is prompted.

**Given** the app is backgrounded for 5 minutes or more
**When** I resume it
**Then** re-authentication is always prompted, regardless of any user setting — this value is fixed, not user-configurable.
